title: Strategy spec
description: A strategy the runtime may trade: what to run, with what parameters, sized how, and the backtest that earned it the right. Emitted by research, consumed by the Go runtime. The runtime refuses any spec missing provenance, with oos_sharpe under 1.0, or older than ttl_days.

strategy.description: Must match a registered Go and Python implementation.

params.description: Strategy-specific. pairs_zscore takes hedge_ratio, lookback, entry_z, exit_z, max_hold_days. ratio_reversion takes lookback, entry_z, exit_z, max_hold_days. sma_trend takes lookback, band. dual_momentum takes lookback, top_k, rebalance_days. time_series_momentum takes lookback, rebalance_days. donchian_breakout takes entry_lookback, exit_lookback.

execution.description: When the signal is read and when the order fills (docs/CONTRACTS.md, Execution). A spec without this block fills at the same close the signal was read at, which is the loop the first four strategies were researched with; every spec research writes now says so explicitly.

research_study.description: The study script that produced the spec (server/internal/research knows it by this name), so a spec is re-validated by the study that earned it, not guessed from the strategy: one strategy can serve several studies.
